title: Minimum Number of Changes to Make Binary String Beautiful
summary: Given a binary string of even length, determine the least number of character changes needed to make the string beautiful, where a string is beautiful if it can be divided into substrings of even length containing only identical characters.
statement: Given a binary string of even length, determine the least number of character changes needed to make the string beautiful, where a string is beautiful if it can be divided into substrings of even length containing only identical characters.
constraints: A beautiful result can be divided into even-length blocks of equal characters.
Return the fewest single-character changes needed.
reference_solution:
def minimum_beautiful_binary_changes(s):
    return sum(s[i]!=s[i+1] for i in range(0,len(s),2))
hints: Any valid even-block partition respects the fixed pairs (0,1),(2,3), and so on.
A mismatched pair needs exactly one change; a matched pair needs none.
After fixing each pair, grouping adjacent equal pairs into larger even blocks is always valid.

tests.explanation: Both pairs 10 and 01 need one change, totaling two.
